data.abstract: Accurate story point estimation is critical for Agile sprint planning, but traditional methods are often inconsistent and machine learning alternatives can be overly complex. We propose a simple framework that estimates story points directly from user story descriptions. Our method uses TF-IDF vectorization and Non-Negative Matrix Factorization (NMF) to extract features, followed by k-medoids clustering to group similar issues. Within each cluster, a weighted k-nearest neighbors (k-NN) regression model predicts the story points. We evaluated our approach on a dataset of 21,140 issues from 26 open-source projects. Experimental results demonstrate that adding NMF to the TF-IDF pipeline provides negligible gains in accuracy. However, using weighted k-NN regression—especially with TF - IDF features alone—consistently outperforms simpler estimators like the cluster mean or median. Our findings suggest this streamlined framework offers a practical balance of simplicity and accuracy for Agile teams.

data.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) play a crucial role in software engineering, excelling in tasks like code generation and maintenance. However, existing benchmarks are often narrow in scope, focusing on a specific task and lack a comprehensive evaluation framework that reflects real-world applications. To address these gaps, we introduce CoCo-Bench (Comprehensive Code Benchmark), designed to evaluate LLMs across four critical dimensions: code understanding, code generation, code modification, and code review. These dimensions capture essential developer needs, ensuring a more systematic and representative evaluation. CoCo-Bench includes multiple programming languages and varying task difficulties, with rigorous manual review to ensure data quality and accuracy. Empirical results show that CoCo-Bench aligns with existing benchmarks while uncovering significant variations in model performance, effectively highlighting strengths and weaknesses. By offering a holistic and objective evaluation, CoCo-Bench provides valuable insights to guide future research and technological advancements in code-oriented LLMs, establishing a reliable benchmark for the field.

data.abstract: Given the rapid evolution of business application development in modern-day organizations and industries, an enhanced, scalable solution is the primary characteristic. In this scenario, comprehending the ways in which effective onboarding activities drive the successful implementation of scalable business applications in the long-term is included. This study answers the research questions of how factors such as Artificial Intelligence (AI), Technology Used (TU), and Technology Skill Proficiency (TSP) influence the Developer Productivity (DP), while improving the ability to execute scalable business applications (SBAs). Through a quantitative approach, this research aims at medium and large-scale IT organizations of Sri Lanka, employing a non-random sampling technique. 104 responses were gathered through a five-point Likert scale questionnaire, which was analyzed with Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) using SmartPLS software to investigate the relationships between our key factors of AI, TU, and TSP with their direct connection to DP, and how it ultimately improves SBAs. Conducting this research disclosed the significance of a formal onboarding process on the productivity of software developers in enhancing the SBAs. To conclude, the findings demonstrate that the objectives of the study were fulfilled, the research questions were addressed, and the hypotheses were likewise validated. Our study has shown the importance of proper onboarding practices, which have a significant impact on improving DP and the development of SBAs.

data.venue: arXiv.org

data.abstract: We present a comprehensive real-world evaluation of AI-assisted software development tools deployed at enterprise scale. Over one year, 300 engineers across multiple teams integrated an in-house AI platform (DeputyDev) that combines code generation and automated review capabilities into their daily workflows. Through rigorous cohort analysis, our study demonstrates statistically significant productivity improvements, including an overall 31.8% reduction in PR review cycle time. Developer adoption was strong, with 85% satisfaction for code review features and 93% expressing a desire to continue using the platform. Adoption patterns showed systematic scaling from 4% engagement in month 1 to 83% peak usage by month 6, stabilizing at 60% active engagement. Top adopters achieved a 61% increase in code volume pushed to production, contributing to approximately 30 to 40% of code shipped to production through this tool, accounting for an overall 28% increase in code shipment volume. Unlike controlled benchmark evaluations, our longitudinal analysis provides empirical evidence from production environments, revealing both the transformative potential and practical deployment challenges of integrating AI into enterprise software development workflows.

data.abstract: Modern software development heavily relies on third-party dependencies to reduce workload and improve developer productivity. Given the vast number of dependencies available and the ease of including them in projects, some introduced dependencies are never used, leading to bloated software, longer build times, and increased network bandwidth usage. While several previous studies have examined the prevalence of unused dependencies and their impact on security, it remains unclear how these dependencies are introduced and removed in software projects. This study aims to answer this question through an empirical study involving 3,020 release versions of 417 Java projects. Our analysis shows that unused packages are common in most projects ($52 \%$ of projects), but few releases (9%) introduce new unused dependencies. Among those resolved unused dependencies, $59 \%$ of them were removed and $41 \%$ were used in later versions. Our findings highlight that not all unused dependencies should be removed in practice.

data.abstract: This study introduces a paradigm-independent, cognitive-based complexity (PICC) metric that extends software complexity measurement beyond traditional approaches such as Cyclomatic Complexity. The PICC metric quantifies cognitive load arising from control-flow structure, failure-handling behavior, nesting depth, and concurrent execution, enabling a more comprehensive characterization of software complexity. By explicitly accounting for factors that influence code comprehension, maintainability, and long-term evolution, the proposed metric addresses key limitations in existing measures. The results indicate that PICC consistently produces higher complexity values, reflecting the additional cognitive demands imposed by modern software constructs and multi-paradigm development practices. This work contributes an adaptable and technically grounded metric that strengthens software quality assessment by better aligning measured complexity with developer effort. In practice, PICC can support code reviews, refactoring prioritization, and quality assurance activities by highlighting areas of elevated cognitive burden. More broadly, this research has the potential to inform improved complexity measurement standards and motivate future advances in software engineering metrics and maintainability evaluation.

data.abstract: Code generation with Large Language Models (LLMs) has helped to increase software developer productivity in coding tasks, but has yet to have significant impact on the tasks of software developers that surround this code. In particular, the challenge of infrastructure management remains an open question. We investigate the ability of an LLM agent to construct infrastructure using the Infrastructure as Code (IaC) paradigm. data.abstract: Development bots are used on Github to automate repetitive activities. Such bots communicate with human actors via issue comments and pull request comments. Identifying such bot comments allows to prevent bias in socio-technical studies related to software development. To automate their identification, we propose a classification model based on natural language processing. Starting from a balanced ground-truth dataset of 19,282 PR and issue comments, we encode the comments as vectors using a combination of the bag of words and TF-IDF techniques. We train a range of binary classifiers to predict the type of comment (human or bot) based on this vector representation. A multinomial Naive Bayes classifier provides the best results. Its performance on a test set containing 50% of the data achieves an average precision, recall, and F1 score of 0.88. Although the model shows a promising result on the pull request and issue comments, further work is required to generalize the model on other types of activities, like commit messages and code reviews.

data.title: Retrieval-Augmented Code Review Comment Generation
data.venue: arXiv.org

openAccessPdf.disclaimer: Notice: Paper or abstract available at https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.11591, which is subject to the license by the author or copyright owner provided with this content. Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use.

data.abstract: Automated code review comment generation (RCG) aims to assist developers by automatically producing natural language feedback for code changes. Existing approaches are primarily either generation-based, using pretrained language models, or information retrieval-based (IR), reusing comments from similar past examples. While generation-based methods leverage code-specific pretraining on large code-natural language corpora to learn semantic relationships between code and natural language, they often struggle to generate low-frequency but semantically important tokens due to their probabilistic nature. In contrast, IR-based methods excel at recovering such rare tokens by copying from existing examples but lack flexibility in adapting to new code contexts-for example, when input code contains identifiers or structures not found in the retrieval database. To bridge the gap between generation-based and IR-based methods, this work proposes to leverage retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) for RCG by conditioning pretrained language models on retrieved code-review exemplars. By providing relevant examples that illustrate how similar code has been previously reviewed, the model is better guided to generate accurate review comments. Our evaluation on the Tufano et al. benchmark shows that RAG-based RCG outperforms both generation-based and IR-based RCG. It achieves up to +1.67% higher exact match and +4.25% higher BLEU scores compared to generation-based RCG. It also improves the generation of low-frequency ground-truth tokens by up to 24.01%. We additionally find that performance improves as the number of retrieved exemplars increases.

data.abstract: Code review is a highly important task in the software development lifecycle. However, some of the characteristics of code review hinder practitionersâ?? performance of this task. Code review is considered to be tedious and uninteresting, and includes challenging human aspects, such as collaboration among stakeholders. Despite the many concerns that need to be taken into consideration when performing code review, a comprehensive, formal definition thereof is yet to be determined. In a previous research, a set of formal guidelines for code review was presented, in the context of performing this task in a gamified environment. In this ongoing research, we explore whether the field of software engineering provides a formal definition for code review, and whether a formal definition is needed. The preliminary findings of this research indicate that while the field does provide several definitions for code review, in all that concerns the human aspect of this task, a formal definition is in order. As a response for this need, we present a framework of the task of code review toward its formalization, embedding gamification for motivation enhancement.

data.abstract:
Purpose. To justify and implement a comprehensive approach to assessing the productivity of software developers, aimed at improving the efficiency of project development management and optimising teamwork processes.
Methods. Modern methods for assessing the productivity of software developers have been analysed, and a mathematical model of a comprehensive productivity indicator has been developed, taking into account weighting coefficients and the normalisation of indicators. An intelligent information system has been developed that integrates with existing development tools, namely version control systems, development environments and team collaboration platforms, and enables the collection, storage and processing of productivity metrics. The GitHub platform was used to test the system, and an assessment of three developers was conducted over a specific period.
Results. The developed intelligent system calculates a comprehensive productivity metric that integrates three groups of metrics: quantitative, communicative and qualitative. Experimental results showed that the comprehensive approach allows for the dynamics of metric changes to be taken into account, reduces the subjectivity of the assessment, and clearly demonstrates the productivity of individual developers and the team as a whole. According to the results, the actual productivity of the team under study was 69.4% of the maximum possible value.
Scientific novelty. A comprehensive approach to assessing the productivity of software developers has been proposed, integrating quantitative, communicative and qualitative metrics, which allows for a more objective evaluation of the work of developers and project teams. The developed mathematical model of a comprehensive productivity indicator, utilising normalisation, ranking and weighting coefficients, represents a new approach to the systematic analysis of productivity in the context of modern software development.
Practical implications. An intelligent system for evaluating software developers’ productivity enables project managers to monitor team performance, identify issues in a timely manner and plan measures to improve productivity. The use of a comprehensive approach contributes to improved project management, developer motivation and the optimisation of software development costs.
Keywords: software, developers, comprehensive approach, performance evaluation, metrics.

data.abstract: Code clones are a well-known source of technical debt, often degrading software maintainability. Modern AI coding assistants can unintentionally introduce clones or even licenseincompatible code, posing maintenance and legal challenges. This research proposes a Large Language Model (LLM)-powered clone refactoring assistant that proactively detects duplicative code during development and suggests high-level refactorings. By bridging traditional clone detection with LLM-driven code generation or transformation, the approach aims to remove redundancies early while ensuring changes remain behavior preserving and legally compliant. The assistant will integrate into development workflows to prevent clone propagation, flag potential intellectual property risks, and incorporate developer feedback for explainable, trustworthy operation. We will evaluate its impact on code quality and developer productivity, and assess how AI enhancements influence long-term maintenance efforts.
